audits.resolution_reason: Negative reachability branch is excluded by sampler/validator, so all-positive lessons fail to distinguish unconditional recoloring. Reviewer-reported Racket counterexample is outside current sampler domain; repair needs a coverage/domain decision, not a changed reference rule.
audits.text:
## 530e5e07db4c

**Reproduced teaching shortcut.** The intended rule recolors gray `5` cells
reachable from the red `2` only when that component also reaches the blue `3`.
The generator's ordinary sampler always constructs a connected `2`→`3` path,
and `self_check` rejects the disconnected branch.  Therefore the simpler rival
“recolor every non-isolated `5` to `4`” fits all sampled lessons without testing
the reachability condition.

I sampled 120 ordinary draws (40 per difficulty); all 120 reached the `3`, and
none exercised the negative branch.  The exact counterexample in
`checks/audit/530e5e07db4c/disconnected-input.json` contains a `2`-connected
three-cell component separated from the `3`.  The selected Racket authority
(hash `f97778fc4cf2`) leaves the entire input unchanged, while the shortcut
recolors the two connected `5` cells.  The source-bound authority output is
`checks/audit/530e5e07db4c/disconnected-racket.json`; the comparison and sampler
counts are in `checks/audit/audit-probe.json`.

The audited source hash is
`940584acdaf6e4e0d4ac65070f1e3be7262ea321a9c39052273e6e87bcaccc64`.
Additional public diagnostics independently report a missing `RULE_HASH`,
texture-domain overlap, rule/source divergence, and more than 17,000 displayed
override findings; see `checks/audit/530e5e07db4c/lint.console.log`,
`defect_lint.console.log`, and `override.console.log`.  I did not modify the
audited generator.

triage.reason: Retain two source-bound findings-only audits: rejected negative reachability branch and canonical tied-size contradiction; neither target repaired. Reviewer-reported evidence only.
